institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The city and the specific host university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Sciences Po sent me very many emails with practical informations of various kinds, which made it somewhat easier to get the necessary upon arrival. We were also a larger group of students from KU, and we helped each other quite a lot.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a introductory week and a "meet the campus"-day

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I stayed at the Fondation Danoise (Det Danske Studenterhus), which I liked a lot. I would recommend it anyone, both introverted and extroverted people as you can take part in the social activities to the extent that you like, and the facilities are really nice. If you choose to apply I recommend putting an effort into writing a good application, as there are quite a lot of Political Science students from KU applying, and my impression is that they want students living here from various academic backgrounds, so competition is tough.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of scammers. The best way to find housing, if you are not staying at Fondation Danoise, is to meet up with potential landlords in person.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All the courses a full within the first minut of course registration, so be ready and have a lot of courses pre-approved, so you can opt for your 2., 3. or even 4. priorities.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The course registration opened at 10.35 on a specific date in July. Then it is first come, first served. It was not very clear from the emails, but it is possible to change courses upon arrival if you have a valid reason I think.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You will receive a comprehensive guide on how to be an exchange student at Sciences Po, which contains all the information (and more) that you need.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 4 out of 5 of the courses that I wanted, so somewhat successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get as many courses pre-approved as possible - especially for the courses you want as substitutes for the obligatory courses at KU. And be aware that if the course says that a part of the validation is a "Final Exam" this usually means that it is a written in-hand sit-in exam.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The workload is much higher than at KU during the semester. You have to submit small essays and do presentations in all of your classes typically. However, my impression is that while it is hard get very high grades (the grade "20" is reserved for God, as some professors put it), it is not that hard to get decent grades or just pass.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The professor is much more in charge of the course. There is no external control, it seems. The quality of the courses therefore varies a lot. Generally, the teaching style is much more unstructured and messy, compared to UCPH. They also do not have the same strong focus on learning theories, as we do in UCPH. They focus more on descriptive knowledge and that your academic arguments are sound and original.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Comparative Politics
2. European Integration and Its Challenges
3. The European Union as an Area of Freedom, Security and Justice
4. The war on terror, a war on screen
5. Money in the Age of Cryptocurrencies

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The teaching in European Union and Its Challenges is not that nice, so if you can get around that course in some way I would recommend doing so. Also the workload in that course is higher than in all other courses I have had.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping is more expensive than you expect, and I ended up buying an additional suitcase on the day of departure

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Dining-out is relatively cheaper than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have a lot of sport offers.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sports. I did boxing and liked it alot. It is a great way to get some French-speaking friends, because most of the English courses contains primarily international students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There is a lot to do in Paris, so I will not try to list everything here. However, I can ensure you that you will not be bored.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The local students are very friendly, but they do not break the ice. So if you want some new friends, you most likely have to approach them first.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Language barrier is hard

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: There is a really nice vibe. It is quite easy to feel at home.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be aware that the workload at Sciences Po is high, and that you will end up dedicating some of your weekends and weekday evenings on doing school work. 
2. It is a little expensive, so apply for a lot of funding and make a realistic budget
3. Be prepared for the course registation, as other students are brutally fast at registering.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nope.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The experience of a different school system, as well as living in another country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was very over-whelming upon arrival, and there are so many people in this city so you usually always have to stand in line or reserve before hand if you want to go out.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
